title: More fact-source pairs carry a located anchor, so fewer facts of a changed page go to a reader, at no loss of anchor precision
goal: factdiff.py anchors gains a breakdown of unlocated:no-match by provider host and tag kind, and the anchoring rule is changed where that breakdown shows a deterministic cause (units it splits badly, such as tables, code lines or list items; numbers and versions; DER facts, whose backing may be one of several cited passages); the located share of the pairs whose source returned text rises above its value at the sprint's start (6588 of 11676 on 2026-10-10, 56%), and anchor precision, measured as in kb/_self/reports/fact-diff.md on a fresh hand-checked sample of 60 newly located anchors, stays at 90% or above; the before and after counts and the precision sample are recorded in that report with the commands that produced them.
notes: Premise run 2026-10-10: python3 _tools/factdiff.py anchors printed anchors=13571 of 15152 fact-source pairs; located=6588 unlocated:fetch-error=90 unlocated:gone=12 unlocated:no-match=5088 unlocated:not-text=1793. kb/_self/reports/fact-diff.md gives located share by tag (DOC 59%, COMMUNITY 56%, CODE 47%, DER 29% of pairs with text) and by provider (github.com pages 28%, docs.gitlab.com 36%, long tail 33%), and anchor precision about 92% at min_cover 0.40 on 60 checked anchors. Quality premise: the precision probe is a fresh hand-checked sample of anchors the change newly locates, not the 60 the cut-offs were tuned on. A fact with no located anchor on a changed source goes to a reader with its whole page, so each newly located pair moves a fact from page reading to passage review or no model. kb/public/_anchors.csv is rewritten by factdiff.py anchor, never by hand.
